title: csvstat: add a --format option (Node, feature + tests + docs)
prompt:
Add an `--format <json|table|text>` option to the `csvstat` command line tool in this repository.

Both `--format json` and `--format=json` must work, the same way `--columns` already does. The option may appear before or after the file name.

- `text` is the default and must keep producing exactly the output it produces today.
- `json` prints one JSON document, pretty-printed with 2 spaces and followed by a newline. Columns appear in file order, and the stats of a column appear in the order count, min, max, mean, sum. Numbers are rounded the same way as in the text format (at most 4 decimals, trailing zeros dropped) but are JSON numbers, not strings. For `data/sample.csv` it prints exactly:

```
{
  "columns": {
    "price": {
      "count": 3,
      "min": 1.5,
      "max": 4,
      "mean": 2.6667,
      "sum": 8
    },
    "qty": {
      "count": 3,
      "min": 1,
      "max": 10,
      "mean": 4.3333,
      "sum": 13
    }
  }
}
```

- `table` prints a plain-text table: a header row `column | count | min | max | mean | sum`, a separator row, and one row per column. Cells are left-aligned and padded with spaces to the width of the widest cell in their column (header included), cells are joined with ` | `, the separator row has one run of `-` per column as wide as the column, joined with `-|-`, and no line has trailing spaces. For `data/sample.csv` it prints exactly:

```
column | count | min | max | mean   | sum
-------|-------|-----|-----|--------|----
price  | 3     | 1.5 | 4   | 2.6667 | 8
qty    | 3     | 1   | 10  | 4.3333 | 13
```

- Any other value is a usage error: print a message that includes the invalid value to stderr, print nothing to stdout, and exit with code 2.

Also add tests for the new option in a new file `test/format.test.js` (at least 3 tests), update README.md to document the option, and make sure the whole test suite (`npm test`) still passes. Do not change the existing tests.
